titel: Ice stays cold in the microwave
kurz: A glass of water and a glass of ice cubes, microwaved for the same time: the water gets hot, the ice barely melts. That is why frozen food thaws so unevenly.
bild_im_kopf: Like dancers in a crowded lift: the music plays, but nobody can turn.
beobachtung: The water has become noticeably warm. Only a little of the ice has melted, and the meltwater at the bottom is warm while the cubes stay cold.
erklaerung: Microwaves heat by twisting water [[molekuel|molecules]] back and forth. In ice the molecules are trapped in a rigid lattice and can barely turn. Liquid water absorbs the energy much better. As soon as a little ice melts somewhere, that very spot heats up fast. That is how the edges cook during defrosting while the centre is still frozen.
schritte: Fill one glass with ice cubes and the other to the same height with cold water.
Heat only the glass of water for 30 seconds on full power, then feel or measure it.
Then heat only the glass of ice for the same time.
Compare: how warm is the water, and how much ice has melted?
material: a thermometer, if you have one
